content.text: The verifier's substantive review confirms compliant/no-redline is correct; the only gap is that my quote didn't evidence the durational point that the regex flagged. I'll re-submit with a quote that shows the Term-long duration on its face.

input.quote: (ix) it is now and throughout the Term shall comply with all applicable Laws in connection with the operation of its business and the performance of its obligations hereunder or the provision of the Service
input.rationale:
Compliant, at or above the preferred position. Section 9(b) is a live express warranty package from Kubient: the Service "will perform in all material respects to industry standards" (p0034); services "shall comply with the terms of this Agreement and shall be free from errors that materially affect their utility" (p0038); the product and service "shall be free of any viruses, Trojan Horses, worms, time bombs, trap doors, back doors" and similar routines (p0036); and Kubient "is now and throughout the Term shall comply with all applicable Laws" (p0041). That covers the preferred position's substantive elements — professional/industry-standard performance, material conformance, no malicious code, and compliance with laws.

On duration: the warranties in 9(b) are framed as continuing representations, warranties and covenants ("will perform", "shall be free from errors", "throughout the Term") rather than as a fixed post-delivery window. There is therefore no explicit "90 days" or "12 months" figure to extract, which is why a period-matching check reports nothing; this is a drafting-form artifact, not a shortfall. A warranty running for the entire Term (one-year Initial Term with automatic one-year renewals under 4(a)) is longer and better for us than the preferred 12-month/90-day parameters, so no extension is needed and inserting a fixed period would risk shortening our protection.

On the disclaimer: Section 13 (p0062) is double-carved — "Except as expressly set forth herein" and "except for the representations and warranties set forth in this Agreement" — so the "as is" language reaches only implied warranties (merchantability, fitness, course of dealing) and the no-minimum-revenue acknowledgement. The express warranty survives intact and the clause is nowhere near walk-away "AS IS" territory.

Noted but not flagged: there is no express repair / re-performance / refund remedy sentence. That is a sub-element short of the preferred wording rather than a material failure, and its absence favours us — with no exclusive-remedy or monetary cap, we retain full direct-damages recovery, indemnity for breach of warranty (p0051), and the right to terminate on 30 days' uncured material breach (p0016). Adding an exclusive remedy would narrow our rights, so no redline is proposed.
